release.body:
What's new in 1.0.13

Fresh
- Explore got more useful: Popular now has time-period filters, a source toggle, and better surfacing for fresh divine videos.
- Home's For You feed now routes through recommendations, so it should feel less random and more alive.
- Mentions resolve and publish across more surfaces. Profiles, lists, captions, and comments do a better job turning people and links into something tappable.
- The video editor gets a cleaner metadata screen, better clips-library sorting, and audio extraction from your own clips.
- Profile polish keeps moving: banner uploads, staged avatar uploads, verified-account chips, and clearer report flows.
- DMs got a redesigned inbox and conversation screen, plus more reliable outgoing recovery when sends only partially succeed.
- Reports now split child-safety concerns into clearer categories, and bug reports can include image attachments.
- 17 non-English locales are filled out, not just half-there.

Sharper
- The feed is now backed by the native video-player path, with smoother first-frame handling and fewer stale overlays.
- Pause is easier to read, with an always-on pause icon and a toggles pill when playback is paused.
- Audio between editor clips is tighter, and remote audio previews cache better on iOS.
- Notifications route more consistently: replies, unread state, badges, and WebSocket/REST dedupe all got cleaned up.
- Profile and feed performance got another pass: smaller thumbnail decodes, cached blurhash work, fewer polling timers, and less rebuild churn.
- Cache sync is now account-scoped, so switching identities should leave less stale state behind.

Squashed
- Adult-content settings now apply more consistently across playback and profile feeds.
- Unknown moderation labels stop leaking into profile feeds.
- Invite redemption retries transient failures instead of giving up too early.
- Back buttons have a safer fallback when the navigation stack is empty.
- Profile edits preserve arbitrary Kind 0 fields and verified NIP-05 data more reliably.
- Likes, reposts, loops, and interaction counts reset and hydrate more correctly as videos are reused or edited.
- Search, notifications, NIP-05 settings, profile loading, and avatar upload paths got targeted failure handling.
- Android no longer leaves the loading overlay stuck when the first-frame callback stalls.

Quietly looking out for you
- Nostr side effects wait for session readiness before firing.
- Publish failures now distinguish "no relays" from broader publish errors.
- Email addresses are redacted from auth-flow logs.
- CI and build cleanup tightened around iOS, Android, Cloudflare deploy metadata, and old FFmpeg residue.

Loop on.

Crashlytics 1.0.13 still has a fatal network-image load path for a missing remote thumbnail.

Observed in 1.0.13:

- Audit remaining NetworkImage/Image.network call sites and route recoverable 404/network failures through errorBuilder/listener onError or VineCachedImage-style fallback.
- Missing thumbnails/stickers/profile images render a fallback instead of reporting a fatal Crashlytics event.
- Add focused widget tests for the user-facing call sites that can receive remote thumbnails.
- Preserve logging for unexpected image errors, but do not mark normal 404/missing media as app crashes.

issue.title: fix(crashlytics): stop Android FlutterJNI detach renderer crash after video surfaces
issue.body:
## Crashlytics evidence

Crashlytics issue: `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a`

Console: https://console.firebase.google.com/project/openvine-co/crashlytics/app/android:co.openvine.app/issues/d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a?&time=1776614940000:1777219740000

Window queried with Firebase MCP: `2026-04-19T16:09:00Z` to `2026-04-26T16:09:00Z`

Impact in that window:

- Events: 31
- Impacted users: 15
- Sessions: 31
- First seen: `1.0.4`
- Last seen: `1.0.8`
- Signal: regressed; Crashlytics says it was closed on `2026-03-08` and regressed on `2026-03-19` in `1.0.7 (497)`.

Sample event:

- Event: `projects/972941478875/apps/1:972941478875:android:c716006682f92d9444b5fe/events/69EE0CF801F5000127E39EE7C625DF0C_2211500816387455056`
- Event time: `2026-04-26T13:12:38Z`
- App version: `1.0.8 (2513)`
- Device: Moto G Power 2025, Android `16`
- Process state: foreground
- Breadcrumb path: video-editor -> video-metadata -> pooled-video-feed repeated

Exception:

```text
java.lang.RuntimeException: Cannot execute operation because FlutterJNI is not attached to native.
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.ensureAttachedToNative (FlutterJNI.java:515)
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterJNI.scheduleFrame (FlutterJNI.java:1013)
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer.scheduleEngineFrame (FlutterRenderer.java:1324)
at io.flutter.embedding.engine.renderer.FlutterRenderer$ImageReaderSurfaceProducer.onImage (FlutterRenderer.java:633)
at FlutterRenderer$ImageReaderSurfaceProducer$PerImageReader.lambda$new$0 (FlutterRenderer.java:517)
at android.media.ImageReader$1.run (ImageReader.java:951)
```

## Start here

This is not the already-filed back navigation issue by itself. Existing issue #2796/PR #2795 guarded app MethodChannel back navigation after engine detach. This crash is in Flutter renderer / `ImageReaderSurfaceProducer`, probably tied to Android platform views or texture-backed video surfaces still producing frames after engine detach/surface disposal.

Likely code areas:

- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/android/src/main/kotlin/com/divinevideo/divine_video_player/DivineVideoPlayerInstance.kt`
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/android/src/main/kotlin/com/divinevideo/divine_video_player/DivineVideoPlayerViewFactory.kt`
- `mobile/packages/divine_video_player/lib/src/divine_video_player_widget.dart`
- `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player` lifecycle if pooled feed uses platform/texture rendering on Android.
- `mobile/android/app/src/main/kotlin/co/openvine/app/MainActivity.kt` only if engine/activity lifecycle ordering is involved.

Relevant local context:

- `DivineVideoPlayerInstance.dispose()` removes callbacks/listeners and releases `textureEntry`.
- Android platform views use `PlatformViewLink` / `AndroidViewSurface` in `divine_video_player_widget.dart`.
- `DivineVideoPlayerPlugin` pauses players on lifecycle pause/resume but only disposes all on engine detach.

## Investigation requirements

Follow root-cause first. Do not assume the previous FlutterJNI back-button fix covers this.

- Reproduce or instrument Android lifecycle while video editor/metadata and pooled feed surfaces are active.
- Trace whether `ImageReaderSurfaceProducer` corresponds to `Texture` usage, Android hybrid composition, or Flutter engine internals triggered by our video widgets.
- Verify disposal order: Flutter widget removed -> platform view disposed -> ExoPlayer surface cleared -> texture released -> engine detached.
- Confirm whether any `Surface`, `SurfaceTextureEntry`, `PlayerView`, or ExoPlayer instance can emit frame callbacks after the Flutter engine is detached.
- Compare event variants in Crashlytics if needed; there are multiple variants under this same issue.

## Suggested fix direction

Possible areas to validate:

- Ensure every Android video surface clears the player and releases the surface before engine/activity detach.
- Add lifecycle-aware stop/dispose guards for video players on `onDetachedFromActivity`, not only `onDetachedFromEngine`.
- Avoid retaining `PlayerView` / `Surface` references beyond view disposal.
- If using texture output, explicitly detach the video surface and stop rendering before `textureEntry.release()`.

## Verification

- Add Android unit tests where practical around plugin/view dispose ordering.
- Run `mobile/packages/divine_video_player` tests and relevant Android tests.
- Manually test rapid navigation: video editor -> metadata -> pooled feed -> background/foreground -> close app.
- After release, confirm Crashlytics issue `d0cacc633461283e8d04c9463445b58a` stops receiving events.

Console: https://console.firebase.google.com/project/openvine-co/crashlytics/app/ios:co.openvine.app/issues/20c590a7f4c538351b659f8ff5d1e578?&time=1776614940000:1777219740000

- Event time: `2026-04-26T08:52:11Z`
- App version: `1.0.9 (660)`
- Device: iPhone 13 Pro, iOS `18.6.0`
- Process state: background
- Breadcrumb path: app startup -> welcome -> feed first batch received

Crash thread:

```text
Thread: mpv/mpv core (crashed)
at __pthread_kill
at pthread_kill
at abort
at dart::SimpleHashMap::Lookup(void*, unsigned int, bool) (hashmap.cc:22)
at DLRT_GetFfiCallbackMetadata (assert.h:31)
at append_event
at setproperty_fn
at mp_dispatch_queue_process
at mp_wait_events
at run_playloop
at mp_play_files
at core_thread
```

## Start here

Likely code areas:

- `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player/lib/src/controllers/player_pool.dart`
- `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player/lib/src/controllers/video_feed_controller.dart`
- `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player/lib/src/widgets/pooled_video_feed.dart`
- `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player/lib/src/widgets/pooled_video_player.dart`
- Any app lifecycle/background handling for pooled video playback.

There is already code acknowledging related media_kit/mpv FFI lifecycle risk:

- `PlayerPool.stopAll()` mentions native mpv callbacks firing on invalidated Dart FFI handles during hot reload.
- `VideoFeedController.dispose()` tries to remove `Video` widgets before disposing native players.
- The crash is in background process state, so this may not be limited to hot reload.

## Investigation requirements

Follow root-cause first. This issue should not be treated as a generic media_kit crash without proving the lifecycle path.

- Trace all dispose/background paths for pooled players and `VideoController` / `Player` ownership.
- Verify whether native mpv callbacks can still target Dart after controllers/notifiers are disposed or after the app backgrounds.
- Check whether backgrounding should pause/stop pooled playback earlier than current logic.
- Check whether feed/player widgets can be removed while mpv event callbacks are still active.
- Compare the current lifecycle guard comments to actual code paths used in production background transitions.

## Suggested fix direction

Possible areas to validate, not assumptions:

- Add a production lifecycle stop/pause path similar to the existing hot-reload emergency `stopAll()` if background transitions leave mpv callbacks alive.
- Ensure all media_kit stream subscriptions/listeners are cancelled before native player disposal.
- Ensure player disposal is awaited where the widget tree may otherwise tear down first.
- Add defensive guards around callbacks/listeners so stale native events cannot mutate disposed Dart state.

## Verification

- Add a focused pooled player lifecycle test for dispose/background order if possible.
- Run tests under `mobile/packages/pooled_video_player`.
- Manually verify iOS background/foreground while feed playback is active, including rapid app switching.
- After release, confirm Crashlytics issue `20c590a7f4c538351b659f8ff5d1e578` stops receiving events.

issue.body:
Crashlytics 1.0.13 has a cluster of iOS fatal crashes where native video/editor callbacks outlive the Flutter engine or texture lifecycle.

Observed in 1.0.13:
- Crashlytics issue 1b1234966e9b3ee4115f734f9f9a1135: ProVideoEditorPlugin.postProgress, NSInternalInconsistencyException: Sending a message before the FlutterEngine has been run.
- Crashlytics issue d7f31dcbfb97da0bbf92d485de8b311b: FVPEventBridge.sendOrQueue, same FlutterEngine-not-run exception.
- Crashlytics issue 92facabdc6fe409a7daf9be134d23be5: FVPFrameUpdater.displayLinkFired, EXC_BAD_ACCESS while notifying textureFrameAvailable.
- Crashlytics issue 9a3f9d030c6aacc38b26a6472b6c84e7: VideoTextureOutput.deliverFrame(_:), EXC_BAD_ACCESS while notifying textureFrameAvailable.

These are all native callback/texture delivery paths continuing after the engine/player/texture recipient is no longer valid. Existing issues #3411 and #3416 cover adjacent media_kit/mpv and Android FlutterJNI crashes, but I did not find an exact iOS issue for these FVP/ProVideo texture/event callbacks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Native iOS event sinks check engine/channel readiness before posting progress/events.
- CADisplayLink, KVO, frame-output, and texture callbacks are stopped or deregistered before engine/player teardown.
- textureFrameAvailable is never called after the texture registry/engine has been invalidated.
- Add lifecycle regression coverage where practical; at minimum document the teardown ordering and verify with an iOS run that rapidly opens/closes editor/player surfaces.
- Keep this focused on native callback lifecycle; do not bundle unrelated Dart player refactors.

issue.title: fix(crashlytics): snapshot relay pending messages before resend
issue.body:
Crashlytics 1.0.13 shows Relay.onConnected iterating a pending-message list while that list can be mutated.

Observed in 1.0.13:
- Crashlytics issue d631ee3d717e4100ece541806d6e8e1d: 1 nonfatal event, 1 user.
- Error: Concurrent modification during iteration: Instance(length:5) of '_GrowableList'.
- Stack: ListIterator.moveNext -> Relay.onConnected at mobile/packages/nostr_sdk/lib/relay/relay.dart:77.
- Code: Relay.onConnected iterates pendingMessages directly and clears it after the loop around lines 77-89. Sending/resubscribe work can mutate pendingMessages while the loop is active.

This is a small deterministic SDK bug and should be fixable without changing protocol behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- onConnected drains or snapshots pendingMessages before resending so mutations during send do not affect the active iteration.
- Preserve full Nostr payloads and subscription IDs; do not truncate IDs in code, logs, or tests.
- Add a nostr_sdk unit test that mutates/queues a pending message during reconnect and verifies no ConcurrentModificationError occurs.
- Preserve the intended behavior of replaying pending messages exactly once per reconnect.

issue.title: fix(crashlytics): map API category names to existing assets safely
issue.body:
Crashlytics 1.0.13 shows category UI deriving SVG paths that do not exist in the bundle.

Observed in 1.0.13:
- Crashlytics issue 20e5b4c3c153605b2ae2ed5f36bddc40: 2 nonfatal events, 1 user.
- Error: Unable to load asset: assets/categories/beverages.svg.
- The same crash family has also appeared for assets/categories/fighting.svg.
- Code: mobile/lib/widgets/categories/category_visuals.dart derives the SVG path from the raw category string around lines 29-35.
- Assets: mobile/assets/categories contains beverage.svg, but not beverages.svg; it also does not contain fighting.svg.

This is a deterministic app bug: category names from API/model data are not guaranteed to match asset filenames one-to-one.

Acceptance criteria:
- Category asset lookup uses an explicit mapping or existence-safe fallback instead of raw lowercased category text.
- All categories returned by the current app/API either resolve to an existing bundled asset or intentionally show a fallback with no asset-load exception.
- Add a test that validates every known category mapping points to an existing file or a defined fallback.
- Keep UI behavior stable for existing valid category assets.

issue.title: fix(crashlytics): harden recording clip file races
issue.body:
Crashlytics 1.0.13 shows recording/editor file lifecycle races that crash instead of degrading gracefully.

Observed in 1.0.13:
- Crashlytics issue 27db69d108f64aa6dcfc0e63de7a4a85: 2 nonfatal events, 1 user.
- Stack: ListBase.firstWhere -> VideoRecorderNotifier.stopRecording at mobile/lib/providers/video_recorder_provider.dart:898.
- Code: stopRecording looks up the just-recorded clip with firstWhere after async metadata/thumbnail extraction, assuming the clip still exists in the provider list.
- Crashlytics issue ff8b8aeba928e83872f286a74cd9d1b4: 2 nonfatal events, 1 user.
- Stack: VideoEditorRenderService.limitClipDuration at mobile/lib/services/video_editor/video_editor_render_service.dart:479.
- Error: PathNotFoundException deleting a source video under Documents/VID_*.mp4 after a trim output exists.
- Code: limitClipDuration deletes inputFile after output existence checks without first confirming the input still exists.

Both failures are recoverable local-file races. They should not reach Crashlytics as unhandled errors.

Acceptance criteria:
- stopRecording handles the clip being removed/replaced while metadata or thumbnail generation is still pending.
- limitClipDuration only deletes/moves files after existence checks and handles already-missing source files as a controlled outcome.
- Add tests for the missing-clip and missing-source-file paths.
- Preserve useful logging for genuinely failed recording/render work.

issue.title: fix(crashlytics): guard video editor callbacks after unmount
issue.body:
Crashlytics 1.0.13 shows video editor UI callbacks using State after the widget has unmounted.

Observed in 1.0.13:
- Crashlytics issue 31cf5709f8e5360a0e076ef892c6f83f: 5 nonfatal events, 4 users.
- Stack: State.context -> _VideoEditorState._syncMainCapabilities callback at mobile/lib/widgets/video_editor/main_editor/video_editor_canvas.dart:599.
- Code: _syncMainCapabilities schedules addPostFrameCallback around lines 586-610 and then reads context inside the callback without a mounted guard.
- Crashlytics issue bf9cb8b8cd0ae8ba8bd0de7f75c32a16: 2 nonfatal events, 2 users.
- Stack: State.setState -> _AudioSelectionBottomSheetState._togglePlayPause -> _selectSound.
- Code: mobile/lib/widgets/video_editor/audio_editor/audio_selection_bottom_sheet.dart:205-209 calls setState from a finally block after awaiting audio preview work without checking mounted.

These are clear lifecycle bugs caused by async/post-frame UI work outliving the screen/sheet.

Acceptance criteria:
- _syncMainCapabilities checks mounted inside the post-frame callback before reading context or touching providers.
- AudioSelectionBottomSheet checks mounted before all setState calls after awaits, including the finally path.
- Add focused widget tests that dispose the editor/sheet while the callback or audio preview future is still pending.
- Do not add arbitrary delays; the fix should be explicit lifecycle coordination.

issue.title: fix(crashlytics): treat extracted editor audio files as local sources
issue.body:
Crashlytics 1.0.13 shows the video editor sometimes passing a local extracted audio path into the remote-audio loading path.

Observed in 1.0.13:
- Crashlytics issue e81e2bc1d6713fa5d91e7b15a0950e18: 16 nonfatal events, 2 users.
- Error: Invalid argument(s): No host specified in URI /var/mobile/.../extracted_audio_*.wav.
- Stack: _HttpClient.getUrl -> AudioClipPlayer._defaultRemoteAudioFileLoader -> AudioClipPlayer.setClip -> AudioTimingCubit._setClippedAudioSource -> AudioTimingCubit.resumePlayback -> VideoAudioEditorTimingScreen fling handler.
- Code: mobile/lib/blocs/video_editor/audio_timing/audio_timing_cubit.dart builds AudioSourceConfig.network(...) for non-bundled editor audio around lines 216-230.
- Code: mobile/packages/sound_service/lib/src/audio_clip_player.dart only uses local-file handling when config.isFile is true; otherwise it sends the URI to HttpClient.

This is app-owned: a local iOS file path should never reach the network loader.

Acceptance criteria:
- Local absolute paths and file:// URIs produced by editor extraction go through AudioSourceConfig.file.
- Remote audio loading rejects or records a controlled error for non-http(s) URIs without calling HttpClient.openUrl.
- Add focused tests for AudioTimingCubit source selection and AudioClipPlayer URI classification.
- Preserve existing behavior for bundled assets and real http/https remote sounds.

issue.title: fix(crashlytics): initialize list cache storage before watchers
issue.body:
Crashlytics 1.0.13 shows people-list watchers reaching storage before their backing stores are initialized.

Observed in 1.0.13:
- Crashlytics issue 85ef98d4d7247f9c8c333a882ccb0f11: HiveError, 66 nonfatal events, 9 users.
- Stack: HiveImpl.openBox -> peopleListsRepository provider -> LocalPeopleListsCache._box -> LocalPeopleListsCache.watchLists.start.
- Code: mobile/lib/providers/app_providers.dart opens the people-lists Hive box lazily at line 2265, and mobile/packages/people_lists_repository/lib/src/local_people_lists_cache.dart calls that opener from _box at line 49.
- Crashlytics issue 3a7a79d293603be758262e713b2df580: LateInitializationError for CacheSync._dao, 14 nonfatal events, 2 users.
- Stack: CacheSync._driveWatchOne -> CacheSync.watchOne -> MyFollowingBloc._onLoadRequested.
- Code: mobile/packages/cache_sync/lib/src/cache_sync.dart uses a static late CacheDao _dao and reads it from _driveWatchOne around line 149; mobile/lib/blocs/my_following/my_following_bloc.dart starts the watcher from line 64.

These are clear startup/order-of-initialization bugs: list UI can start watchers before Hive/CacheSync are ready.

Acceptance criteria:
- PeopleListsRepository cannot open/watch its Hive box before Hive is initialized for the app environment.
- CacheSync either initializes before any BLoC calls watchOne/watchMany or fails with a controlled, recoverable error that does not report LateInitializationError.
- Add tests for watcher startup before storage readiness.
- Do not paper over this by swallowing all list/cache errors; real storage failures should still be visible in logs/Crashlytics with actionable context.

issue.body:
Crashlytics 1.0.13 shows app-owned async Bloc lifecycle crashes where work completes after the UI has disposed the bloc/cubit.

Observed in 1.0.13:
- Crashlytics issue b06311065575782602a6b48f40dae7b8: 100 nonfatal events, 19 users.
- Stack: _BroadcastStreamController.add -> Bloc.add -> OtherProfileBloc._onLoadRequested.
- Code: mobile/lib/blocs/other_profile/other_profile_bloc.dart calls add(const VerifiedClaimsRequested()) after awaited repository work at lines 79, 82, and 91 without checking whether the bloc has closed.
- Crashlytics issue 5fc836d99d2bb6de099dc829768f9489: 5 nonfatal events, 2 users.
- Stack: BlocBase.emit -> InviteStatusCubit.load at mobile/lib/blocs/invite_status/invite_status_cubit.dart:31.

This is the same bug class as prior closed fixes #3734/#3735 and #3455, but the 1.0.13 evidence points at different owners.

Acceptance criteria:
- OtherProfileBloc does not call add after close when profile loading completes after disposal.
- InviteStatusCubit does not emit after close when invite-status loading completes after disposal.
- Add focused bloc/cubit tests that close the owner before the awaited dependency completes and assert no state error is recorded.
- Keep the fix local to lifecycle handling; do not suppress unrelated repository errors.

issue.title: perf(inbox): remove N+1 latest-message overlay queries in DmRepository
issue.body:
## Summary
PR #4286 adds a read-time workaround in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart` to repair stale inbox preview data by overlaying each conversation row with the actual latest message from `direct_messages`.

That workaround fixes correctness, but it introduces a new performance problem: every emission from `watchAcceptedConversations()` and `watchPotentialRequests()` now performs one `DirectMessagesDao.getMessagesForConversation(..., limit: 1)` query per conversation.

For users with many conversations, this turns a single conversations-stream update into an N+1 fan-out of DAO reads.

## Current implementation
PR #4286 changes these paths:
- `watchAcceptedConversations()` -> `.asyncMap(_overlayLatestMessages)`
- `watchPotentialRequests()` -> `.asyncMap(_overlayLatestMessages)`

`_overlayLatestMessages()` then does:
- iterate every `ConversationRow`
- call `getMessagesForConversation(row.id, limit: 1, ownerPubkey: _ownerPubkey)`
- copy the latest message fields back onto the domain model
- resort the list in memory by the overlaid timestamp

Relevant code in the PR:
- `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart:1667-1698`

## Why this matters
The workaround runs on every stream tick, not just on first load.

That means:
- 10 conversations -> 10 extra DAO reads per emit
- 100 conversations -> 100 extra DAO reads per emit
- every accepted-conversations refresh and every potential-requests refresh pays this cost

Even if the reads are parallelized with `Future.wait`, the app still performs one query per conversation, plus an in-memory resort, on every update. This is avoidable read amplification on a hot inbox path.

## Root cause
The comment added in PR #4286 documents the underlying correctness problem well: the denormalized `conversations.lastMessageContent` / `lastMessageTimestamp` fields can drift out of sync with the real latest message in `direct_messages`.

The overlay is compensating for write-path drift at read time.

## Desired outcome
Keep the correctness fix, but remove the per-conversation query fan-out.

## Candidate fixes
### Option A: batched latest-message query
Add a DAO method that fetches the latest message for many conversation ids in one query, for example:
- `getLatestMessagesForConversations(List<String> conversationIds, {required String ownerPubkey})`

Then replace the N queries in `_overlayLatestMessages()` with a single batched read and a map/join in memory.

### Option B: fix denormalized-column drift at the write path
Investigate why `conversations.lastMessageContent` and `lastMessageTimestamp` become stale during backfill / out-of-order gift-wrap arrival.

If the write path can guarantee the denormalized columns always reflect the actual latest message, the overlay can be removed entirely and the existing conversation-watch queries can remain the source of truth.

### Option C: hybrid transition
Ship a batched DAO read first to remove the N+1 cost, then follow with a write-path correctness fix and delete the overlay once the denormalized columns are trustworthy again.

## Acceptance criteria
- Inbox conversation streams no longer perform one `getMessagesForConversation(... limit: 1)` call per conversation on every emit.
- The inbox preview still shows the true latest message even when the conversation row is stale.
- Ordering remains based on the real latest message timestamp.
- Existing regression coverage for stale preview overlay remains intact or is updated to cover the new batched/corrected implementation.
- If the final fix relies on transitional code, include a linked `TODO(#issue)` with a clear removal plan.

## Regression tests to preserve
The tests added in PR #4286 should remain conceptually covered:
- overlays the latest message from `DirectMessageRow` over the denormalized row preview
- re-sorts conversations by the actual latest message timestamp
- file-message preview overlay behavior

## Context
Introduced while reviewing PR #4286.

This issue tracks removing the new N+1 inbox read-path debt without losing the correctness fix that motivated it.

issue.title: DM: surface swallowed DAO bookkeeping failures in self-wrap recovery paths
issue.body:
## Summary

`DmRepository.recoverSelfWrap` and `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` swallow DAO bookkeeping failures via `Log.error` only. Crashlytics doesn't see them because the wrapped errors are not `Reportable` per `.claude/rules/error_handling.md`. Today we have no signal for how often these doubly-degraded paths fire in production.

## Problem

The doubly-degraded path in `recoverSelfWrap` (publish landed; both `deleteById` and fallback `markSelfWrapStatus(sent)` threw) is documented as safe via NIP-17 receive-side dedup — but "safe" is hypothesis until we measure. Same for any DAO write failure inside the recipient-success finalize path. We currently have no way to know if this is happening 0/day or 100/day.

## Desired Outcome

Surface DAO bookkeeping failures in these recovery paths so they're visible in monitoring without flooding Crashlytics.

## Scope

Decide between:

1. **Wrap as `Reportable`** per the matrix in `.claude/rules/error_handling.md`. These are arguably "programming-invariant violations" once the publish has landed — the row should always be writeable. Risk: Crashlytics noise on transient SQLite contention.
2. **Counter / debug surface only.** Increment a metric, expose under a debug screen. Less noisy, but invisible without proactive checking.
3. **Both.** Counter for triage, `Reportable` only on persistent runs (e.g., N consecutive failures for the same rumor).

## Context

- Two specific call sites today, both in `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/dm_repository.dart`: `recoverSelfWrap` doubly-degraded catch, plus any throw inside `_finalizeAfterRecipientSuccess` (currently upstream of any try/catch on the caller side).
- Spotted during PR #4106 review by Liz; follow-up to #4102.

issue.title: task(dm): durable outgoing-message queue + self-wrap publish failure detection
issue.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #3902 (fixed in #3908). PR #3908 shipped the immediate user-visible fix (clear optimistic on failure, retry SnackBar, BlocProvider keyed on repo identity). Two durability gaps remain and they're the same problem at different layers — file together so the design covers both:

- **C — Durable outgoing-message queue.** In-flight sends only live in `ConversationBloc` memory. Background the app, lock the screen, or pop the conversation while a send is in flight, and the optimistic + the in-flight `await sendMessage` are both lost. There's also no automatic retry on connectivity restoration — only the SnackBar's one-tap manual retry.
- **F3 — Silent self-wrap publish failure** at `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/nip17_message_service.dart:118-132`:
  ```dart
  if (selfWrapEvent != null) {
    await _nostrService.publishEvent(selfWrapEvent);  // result discarded
  }
  ```
  The recipient's gift wrap can publish successfully while the self-addressed wrap silently fails to land. Recipient sees the message; sender's other devices never see it. The current test at `nip17_message_service_test.dart:223` (`returns success even when self-wrap publish throws`) literally pins that bug.

## Why one issue, not two

C is the *durability* layer. F3 is the trigger that makes durability necessary. Without C, F3 has nowhere to surface the partial-failure state to the user. Without F3, C can't tell "fully delivered" from "delivered to recipient only" — which is the difference between deleting the queue row and keeping it for retry.

## Proposed approach (high level)

Mirror the in-repo `PendingActions` / `PendingActionService` precedent (`mobile/packages/db_client/lib/src/database/tables.dart:361` and `mobile/lib/services/pending_action_service.dart`):

- New `outgoing_dms` Drift table — pending-queue row per outgoing rumor with **independent** `recipient_wrap_status` and `self_wrap_status` columns (each enum: pending | sent | failed), `retry_count`, `last_error`, `last_attempt_at`, `owner_pubkey`, `rumor_event_json`. Storing the rumor JSON keeps the rumor id stable across retries — critical for receiver-side dedup.
- `NIP17MessageService.sendPrivateMessage` returns per-wrap status instead of a single bool — surfaces F3.
- `DmRepository.sendMessage` inserts the queue row first, calls the service, updates the row with both statuses; on both-success deletes queue row + inserts `direct_messages` atomically; on either-failure retains the row.
- New `OutgoingDmRetryService` — `PendingActionService`-shaped, listens to connectivity, replays failed rows with exponential backoff (steal `PendingActionRetryConfig` defaults: 5 retries, 2s → 5min, 2× backoff).
- `ConversationBloc` switches to `Rx.combineLatest2(watchMessages, watchOutgoing)`. State carries a `Map<String, MessageDeliveryStatus>` keyed by rumor id — the existing `state.messages` list is unchanged in shape, status flows through a parallel map (avoids polluting `DmMessage` with delivery state, keeps `state_management.md` rules intact).
- `MessageBubble` renders WhatsApp-style indicators (clock / single check / double check / error / cancelled). Long-press on failed surfaces Retry + Cancel actions in the existing `MessageActionsSheet`.

The existing `lastFailedSend` SnackBar from PR #3908 stays as the synchronous "fail-fast retry while the input is still in your head" affordance. The queue handles the asynchronous "eventually failed or partially succeeded, recoverable later" cases. Both can fire on the same failure — tests pin the no-double-publish invariant.

## Architecture, files, tests, risks

Full plan with bottom-up implementation order (Client → Repo → Service → BLoC → UI), affected-files table, layer-by-layer test strategy, and a risks section (rumor id stability across retries, half-delivered UX, backoff tuning, multi-account isolation, schema-version-1 + `_createMissingTables` upgrade path) is in the PR thread on #3908. Will be moved here when the work begins.

## Out of scope

- **Approach D** from the original investigation (split persisted vs. optimistic into separate state fields). Once C ships, the queue's per-row status IS the principled split — D folds into C for free.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An outgoing DM survives the app being killed mid-send and reaches the relay automatically when connectivity returns.
- [ ] A DM whose recipient wrap succeeded but self wrap failed is visibly distinguished in the conversation, with a recoverable action that re-attempts only the missing publish (no double-deliver to the recipient).
- [ ] All existing #3908 tests + bloc + view tests stay green.
- [ ] New tests (DAO, repo, service, bloc, view, migration) cover the matrix above.
- [ ] No regression in the SnackBar retry flow shipped by #3908.

## References

- Original Zendesk-imported bug: #3902 ("Inconvenience with sending and receiving DMs")
- Immediate fix: #3908
- In-repo precedent: `PendingActions` table + `PendingActionService` (likes/reposts/follows offline queue)
- Self-wrap site: `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/nip17_message_service.dart:118-132`
- NIP-17 spec: gift wrap (kind 1059) → seal (kind 13) → rumor (kind 14/15)
